words.connector: Think of App Engine like a fully-managed apartment building — you move in your furniture (code) and the building management handles utilities, maintenance, and adding floors when more tenants arrive, but the apartment layout is prescribed.
words.techContext: Our legacy admin dashboard still runs on App Engine Standard — it predates Cloud Run, and the migration cost exceeds the benefit for a low-traffic internal tool, so it remains on the platform it was born on.
words.exampleSentence: App Engine's built-in traffic splitting let us gradually shift 10% of requests to the new version of our service while keeping 90% on the stable version, with zero changes to our load balancer configuration.

codeExample.code:
# app.yaml — App Engine Standard configuration
runtime: python311
service: default

automatic_scaling:
  min_instances: 0
  max_instances: 10
  target_cpu_utilization: 0.65

env_variables:
  DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://...' 

handlers:
  - url: /.*
    script: auto

words.etymology: App Engine — App as shorthand for application; Engine as a metaphor for a powerful processing system; launched at Google I/O 2008 as Google's first cloud offering, predating the term 'cloud computing' becoming mainstream.

words.shortDefinition: GCP's unified AI platform — a single managed environment for training, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models and accessing Google's foundation models.
words.simpleDefinition: Vertex AI is GCP's one-stop shop for machine learning. It provides managed infrastructure for training custom models (on CPUs, GPUs, or TPUs), serving predictions at scale, running ML pipelines, and accessing Google's foundation models (Gemini, Imagen) via API. It unifies what were previously separate GCP ML services under a single platform with a consistent API and UI.
words.longDefinition: Vertex AI was launched in 2021 as Google Cloud's unified ML platform, consolidating previously separate products (AI Platform, AutoML, Notebooks) under a single API and experience. It covers the full ML lifecycle: data labeling, feature engineering (Feature Store), managed Jupyter notebooks (Workbench), distributed training (Training, supporting TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, and XGBoost), model evaluation, hyperparameter tuning, and online/batch prediction serving (Endpoints). For teams without ML expertise, AutoML provides no-code model training for structured data, image, text, and video tasks. Model Garden provides access to Google's first-party foundation models (Gemini, Imagen, Chirp) and hundreds of open-source models (Llama, Mistral) via a managed API. Vertex AI Pipelines enables ML workflow orchestration using Kubeflow Pipelines components. Vector Search provides managed embedding retrieval for RAG and semantic search. The platform targets teams that want managed ML infrastructure on GCP without operating their own Kubernetes clusters for ML workloads.
words.connector: Think of Vertex AI like a well-equipped research laboratory that also has a factory floor — the lab handles experiments and model development, the factory scales successful experiments into production prediction services, and the library (Model Garden) provides pre-built starting points.
words.techContext: We use Vertex AI for three things: Gemini API for our document summarization feature, AutoML to classify support tickets without writing any model code, and Vertex AI Endpoints to serve our fine-tuned text classifier with a managed autoscaling REST API.
words.exampleSentence: Migrating from a self-managed Kubernetes cluster running TensorFlow Serving to Vertex AI Endpoints cut our ML infrastructure operational burden from half an engineer's time to essentially zero while providing better autoscaling.

codeExample.code:
# Deploy a model to a Vertex AI endpoint
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project='my-project', location='us-central1')

# Upload a model from Cloud Storage
model = aiplatform.Model.upload(
    display_name='my-classifier',
    artifact_uri='gs://my-bucket/models/classifier/',
    serving_container_image_uri='us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/sklearn-cpu.1-3:latest',
)

# Deploy to an endpoint
endpoint = model.deploy(machine_type='n1-standard-4')
prediction = endpoint.predict(instances=[[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]])

words.etymology: Vertex from Latin vertex ('highest point, crown of the head, peak'); in graph theory a vertex is a node in a network — suggesting connectivity between AI components; AI for Artificial Intelligence; the product name was chosen when the platform consolidated GCP's ML services at Google Cloud Next 2021.
